summary: Preserved candidate PR 2581 and corrected both independently reviewed counterexamples: per-call streaming overflow is enforced even after an earlier complete call, finish releases held text and resets state, and non-streaming detection accepts singular K2-Thinking section markers.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: the mixed complete/unclosed increment emitted two call fragments and retained 269 characters through finish; singular non-streaming input returned no calls and leaked all marked text.
Focused detector suite including candidate regressions and new mixed-overflow, finish, and singular non-streaming cases: 70 passed and 7 subtests passed.
Existing parser integration coverage: 6 passed, 237 deselected.

Passing-after reproduction: one complete call was emitted, the unclosed second call was released as 222 normal characters with an empty buffer, finish retained nothing, and singular non-streaming input parsed one call with prefix content preserved.
No whitespace errors in the consolidated patch.

gpu_execution.evidence: The corrected code is deterministic Python string parsing. No Kimi-K2/K2.5 weights were available, so GPU/model execution would not validate these source-level counterexamples.

remaining_limitations: No Kimi-K2 or Kimi-K2.5 weights were available; actual model token emission, semantic tool accuracy, HTTP/client behavior, and distributed execution remain unverified.
No native code changed and repository-environment.json declares native and wheel artifacts null, so no native rebuild applies.

The configured section limit continues to use Python character count, matching the preserved candidate implementation; multibyte byte-memory accounting was not part of either concrete review counterexample.
